evidence.claim: Booking Holdings describes itself as a leading provider of online travel and related services through brands including Booking.com, Priceline, Agoda, KAYAK and OpenTable, serving consumers and local partners in more than 220 countries and territories.
As of the finance snapshot gathered on 2026-06-09, Booking Holdings had a market capitalization of about $128.9 billion, supporting the mega-cap reference-lane classification.

Sabre's 2025 annual report describes the company as providing global travel solutions for travel suppliers and travel buyers through a B2B travel marketplace, global distribution network and related solutions.

Sabre announced a definitive agreement to sell its Hospitality Solutions business to TPG for $1.1 billion while stating that hotel B2B distribution remained a strategic area and that the divestiture would focus Sabre on airline IT and travel marketplace platforms.
evidence.source_title: Sabre enters into definitive agreement to sell its Hospitality Solutions business unit to TPG for $1.1 billion

evidence.claim: As of the finance snapshot gathered on 2026-06-09, Sabre had a market capitalization of about $658 million, supporting the 300m-to-1b small-cap discovery classification.

Agilysys describes its hospitality software coverage as serving hotel brands, independent hotels, resorts, management companies, cruise lines, airports, restaurants and gaming properties, with products including property management and point-of-sale systems.

A 2026 filing summary reports Agilysys FY2026 revenue of $319.3 million, up from $275.6 million in FY2025, driven mainly by subscription, maintenance and professional services tied to hospitality software.

evidence.claim: As of the finance snapshot gathered on 2026-06-09, Agilysys had a market capitalization of about $2.53 billion, supporting the mid-cap discovery classification.

evidence.claim: Third-party market-cap sources cited PROS Holdings at approximately $1.12 billion as of late May or early June 2026, supporting the above-$1B small-cap discovery classification.

memory_update.text: For the travel marketplace and hotel distribution tollbooth node, maintain Booking Holdings only as a reference leader; do not let it crowd out infrastructure names in later layers.

Sabre is a high-relevance but messy underfollowed candidate: post-2025 Hospitality Solutions divestiture exposure must be validated around retained B2B travel marketplace and hotel B2B distribution, not legacy SynXis assumptions.
Agilysys is a plausible underfollowed hotel operating-software chokepoint candidate; next layer should test whether PMS/POS/payments integrations create switching costs and recurring SaaS economics.

PROS is an adjacent travel-distribution infrastructure candidate with stronger airline than hotel exposure; include only if the funnel allows airline offer/pricing rails as part of the broader travel marketplace tollbooth layer.

Several seemingly pure hotel-channel-manager or travel-data names are not US-listed or are private/non-US listed, including SiteMinder, RateGain, Sojern/Adara and the carved-out Sabre Hospitality/Aven entity. Later passes should decide whether non-US listings are permitted.

node: Travel marketplace and hotel distribution tollbooths
summary: Layer 1B expands the US-listed universe around travel distribution chokepoints rather than hotel ownership. The reference anchor is Booking Holdings as the obvious two-sided lodging marketplace. The underfollowed lane is concentrated in smaller travel infrastructure names: Sabre as a B2B travel marketplace/GDS and hotel B2B distribution provider after divesting Hospitality Solutions; Agilysys as hospitality operating software embedded inside hotels, resorts, casinos and cruise lines; and PROS as airline offer/pricing infrastructure that supports dynamic pricing, direct distribution and conversion across channels. These are not buy/sell recommendations. They are research candidates for later evidence testing around supplier density, switching costs, recurring revenue, take rate, customer concentration and travel-cycle sensitivity.
